holidays.name: National Vinyl Record Day
holidays.description: Dig out the turntable and give your dusty crate of records a spin. This day celebrates the warm crackle, big album art and ritual of dropping the needle on a favorite LP.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance, and it is tied to the August 12, 1877 date when Thomas Edison is said to have first demonstrated sound recording with his tinfoil phonograph.
holidays.funFact: Edison's first recording is said to have been the nursery rhyme 'Mary Had a Little Lamb'. It was captured on a sheet of tinfoil wrapped around a cylinder.

holidays.name: National Middle Child Day
holidays.description: This day is for the overlooked, the peacemakers and the kids who got the hand-me-downs. Middle children get their moment in the spotlight, and a little recognition from their siblings.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular yearly nod to the sibling stuck between the oldest and the baby.
holidays.funFact: Middle-child syndrome is a popular idea, but researchers have found little hard evidence for it. Plenty of famous achievers were middle children, though.

holidays.name: National Gooey Butter Cake Day
holidays.description: Celebrate a dessert that is rich, buttery and a little bit sinful, with a chewy, custardy filling on a soft base and a dusting of powdered sugar. It is a St. Louis classic that deserves a bigger fan base.
holidays.origin: Gooey butter cake is a St. Louis specialty. Legend says it came from a baker's mistake in the 1930s, when the wrong ratio of ingredients made a cake that turned out delightfully dense. The day itself is an unofficial observance.
holidays.funFact: In St. Louis, gooey butter cake is a beloved local specialty. It is often sold in bakeries and grocery stores, and many locals eat it at breakfast.
